issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object. The template contains TODOs for this method but no signature, which combined with the UML leads students to implement an int-returning method; the solution's use of a custom StudentCount type is not described in the problem and introduces a type mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount class, or (B) update the problem statement UML and the template to introduce and document the StudentCount type and change the UML return type to StudentCount so students are aware of and can use the custom type. Ensure the template method signature matches the chosen approach.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (a primitive int) while the solution implementation returns a StudentCount object (class name StudentCount) from getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) for the same conceptual entity 'total number of students' and changes its representation across artifacts, creating confusion for students expecting an int as shown in the UML and task description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation consistent: either change the problem statement/UML to indicate getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a StudentCount (and document the StudentCount class) or modify the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (remove or avoid using the StudentCount class). Prefer aligning the solution with the UML (return int) to avoid introducing a new type not mentioned in the exercise.
